name: Bored Bakry
description: Bakry got bored of solving problems related to xor, so he asked you to solve this problem for him. You are given an array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ integers $$$[a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n]$$$. Let's call a subarray $$$a_{l}, a_{l+1}, a_{l+2}, \ldots, a_r$$$ good if $$$a_l \, \& \, a_{l+1} \, \& \, a_{l+2} \, \ldots \, \& \, a_r \gt a_l \oplus a_{l+1} \oplus a_{l+2} \ldots \oplus a_r$$$, where $$$\oplus$$$ denotes the bitwise XOR operation and $$$\&$$$ denotes the bitwise AND operation . Find the length of the longest good subarray of $$$a$$$, or determine that no such subarray exists.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^6$$$) — the length of the array. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^6$$$) — elements of the array.
output_specification: Print a single integer — the length of the longest good subarray. If there are no good subarrays, print $$$0$$$.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1592E — Bored Bakry [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
